_doc: Per-source expectations for sanity checks. type drives which check matters:
feed     - new ids should appear across a real polling interval; novelty ~0 over
several intervals means the extract window is stuck or the source stalled
status   - same ids every run, VALUES drift; value_keys are the fields expected to
change across a real interval (freeze = upstream or extract problem)
snapshot - periodic full snapshot (charts, catalogs); content changes slowly, only
staleness and record-count stability are meaningful
expected_gap_minutes mirrors the yml cron; stale = last run age > 2x gap + 10min.

sec_edgar.notes: novelty drops to ~0 outside US market hours and on weekends; that is normal

certificate_transparency.notes: crt.sh search over wikipedia.org's cert history; new certs appear ~monthly, identical output day to day is normal

ripe_ris_live.notes: streaming sample; every run should be ~100% novel

discourse_meta.notes: latest-topics window: ids persist while views/bumps drift, new topics enter as created; novelty ~0 on quiet hours is normal

onionoo.notes: per-record 'published' is the hourly consensus timestamp: ~1.0 value change across publishes is HEALTHY, 0.0 across >1h means a stale bulletin

gh_archive.notes: live tail; every run should be ~100% novel

deezer.notes: chart snapshot; rank/position churn between runs is the signal

tatoeba.notes: small volunteer project; hours with zero new eng-fra sentence pairs are normal, a full day of zero novelty is not

musicbrainz.notes: returns 503 under load as designed rate-limiting; an isolated failed hourly run is normal, a streak is not

launch_library.notes: upcoming launches; ids persist while net/status fields revise

celestrak_socrates.notes: celestrak.org is slow serving the 16MB file; occasional connect timeouts observed (2026-09-03), retries=2 in yml; a single missed run of 3/day is tolerable

rcsb_pdb.notes: weekly release batches; several identical daily runs then a burst is normal

pubchem.notes: DISABLED 2026-09-03: static lookup, not a change feed

gutendex.notes: download_count drifts daily on a stable book set

nsidc_sea_ice.notes: one new row per day; same-day reruns show 0 novelty and that is normal

gdelt_doc.notes: backed off from 15min to hourly cadence 2026-09-04 after sustained 429s; a handful of scattered 429s is expected etiquette-friction, but consecutive_failures climbing again means the block is back

job_boards_greenhouse.notes: named-company ATS boards; postings churn slowly, so low id_novelty between daily runs is normal. Isolated board failures are expected catalog drift (companies migrate ATS); the task only fails when a provider-wide outage takes out ~all boards

job_boards_lever.notes: see job_boards_greenhouse; slow posting churn, isolated board failures tolerated

job_boards_ashby.notes: see job_boards_greenhouse; also carries structured compensation where companies publish it

job_boards_smartrecruiters.notes: large global non-tech employers; a few board failures per run are normal at this catalog size

job_boards_workable.notes: DISABLED 2026-09-04: upstream returns Cloudflare 1015 to this host after catalog discovery. Expect no runs until it is re-verified and re-enabled

job_boards_recruitee.notes: Benelux/Nordic SMEs; 429s appear if the source is run repeatedly by hand, not at the daily cadence

job_boards_personio.notes: German-speaking SMEs over XML; deliberately throttled to 2 concurrent requests with a 600ms gap because Personio 429s easily

job_boards_breezy.notes: smallest provider in the catalog (single verified board); a low record count is expected, not a fault

job_boards_rippling.notes: see job_boards_greenhouse; small catalog, slow churn

job_boards_workday.notes: largest provider: ~875 tenants, ~220k postings, ~45min per run. A handful of tenant failures per run is normal drift; postedOn is relative text from upstream, not a timestamp

job_feed_themuse.notes: newest 99 pages of a much larger index; page 100 is rejected by the API, which is why the cap is 99

job_feed_arbeitnow.notes: capped at 8 pages; the API 429s around the tenth rapid page, so a 429 here means the cap needs lowering rather than a retry

job_feed_getonboard.notes: Latin America and remote roles; feed currently fits in ~3 pages, so record counts near 200 are normal

job_feed_remotive.notes: single full response; record count tracks the size of the live remote board

job_feed_remoteok.notes: single full response; the API's first row is terms metadata and is intentionally skipped

job_feed_himalayas.notes: cursor-paginated; capped at 100 cursors (~2000 newest of ~102k indexed roles)

job_feed_jobicy.notes: newest 50 remote roles per run; steady ~50 record count is expected

job_feed_workingnomads.notes: single full response of currently listed remote roles

job_feed_weworkremotely.notes: RSS feed; titles arrive as 'Company: Role' and are split on extract
